sentences.text:
This is second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, for grant of bail relating to FIR/Crime No.801/2022 dated 13.11.2022 registered at Police Station Garha, District Jabalpur, for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 406, 467,
468, 471 r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 25.09.2023 and the trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.

The applicant is the permanent resident of district and there is no possibility of his absconding or Raj Singh Thakur vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99506875/

He is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
5.
This is repeat bail application on behalf of applicant.
Earlier one was dismissed vide order dated 26.10.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.45921/2023 with liberty to renew the prayer after filing of the charge-sheet.

Now it has been argued that the charge-sheet has been filed and bail has been granted to other accused persons including Yogesh Sharma in M.Cr.C. No.54069/2023.
6.
According to applicant, he was working as choukidar in the concerned petrol pump and he has been arrayed as an accused on the basis of memorandum of other accused.
It has also been argued that no recovery has been made from his possession nor any bill signed by him was seized.

Earlier he was given a notice under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C.
7.
This bail application has been opposed by the State.
8. Case diary reveals that no recovery was made from the applicant.
Although, some receipts issued by petrol pump were seized in the matter, but those documents have not been sent for hand writing examination to show involvement of applicant in the crime.

Further, it has been claimed in the charge- sheet that applicant and other accused persons jointly deposited a part of defalcated amount, but no document regarding this deposit has been seized and filed along with the charge-sheet.

9. Having considered all these facts, this Court finds it appropriate to release the applicant on bail,
therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this bail application is allowed.

10. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for her appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.

11. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
12.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
